target_customer: Microbiology labs in food, agriculture, pharma and biotech that count and prepare bacterial plates
problem: Microbiologists spend hours on manual plate filling and colony counting; Reshape sells single-function robots and image analysis instead of one all-purpose lab robot.
business_model: Hardware sales plus software and consumables for lab automation
product_category: Lab automation robotics and computer vision

founders.name: Carl-Emil Grøn Fuglesang
education: Mechanical engineer and physicist per YC page; school not stated
founders.background_notes: Listed as Carl-Emil Grøn in TechCrunch April 2024.

founders.name: Magnus Nyborg Madsen
founders.background_notes: YC page: robotics and automation for life-science R&D.

founders.name: Daniel Storgaard
founders.background_notes: YC page: development, project management, testing, customer communication and finance.

competitors.name: Interscience
competitors.what: Automatic platers and colony counters sold as a Plate and Count system for microbiology labs

competitors.name: Synbiosis
competitors.what: Automated colony counters and ProtoCOL software with a pour plate module

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom robotics, mechatronics and machine learning image analysis for biological plates, requiring hardware reliability and lab validation from a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus image data from customer plates create some barriers, but colony counting is an established product category with long-lived vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying reported through 2025; the company raised a $20M Series A in April 2024.

market_need_then: Microbiology plate work was manual and repetitive, and the YC pitch said existing all-purpose lab robots sat unused. No quantified 2021 demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses reshapebiotech.com; the name is shared with ReShape Lifesciences, a bariatric device maker.

identity.logo: Three solid orange circles in a triangle, per a third party logo aggregator (unverified)

brand_strength.rationale: Clear but generic name that collides with an unrelated public medical company; press about Denmark's largest seed round gave visibility, but no brand driven growth is documented.

outcome_analysis: Reshape Biotech has grown from a 2021 Copenhagen YC company into a funded robotics firm with an $8.1M seed in February 2023 that was described as Denmark's largest, followed by a $20M Series A led by Astanor in April 2024. Its strength is single-function robots and image analysis aimed at a manual workflow, while its generic name collides with an unrelated listed company.
notes: A small seed of about $980K or kr6M in May 2021 appears only in aggregators and is left out as unverified. Silicon Canals reported the 2023 round as EUR 7.5M. Founding year is 2018 per YC and 2019 in one aggregator. The company blog post and website could not be fetched (domain safety check rate limited), so the Series A is sourced to tech.eu and search results naming company, Arctic Startup and TechCrunch. Competitor sources are current product pages that are undated, so presence in 2021 is not date verified; Interscience and Synbiosis are long-established vendors. Search for layoffs returned only the unrelated ReShape Lifesciences. Founder education and prior employers not found.
